label: TP
reason: User-supplied query string parameter flows directly into cookie name construction via concatenation ('user' + testCaseNumber), which includes the test class name containing the parameter. The resulting cookie name is printed unescaped to HTML response ('whose value is: '+rememberMe.getValue()). While HtmlUtils.htmlEscape is called on 'bar', it is used for a different purpose (random key generation context) and does not sanitize the cookie name printed to the response. An attacker can inject script tags into the cookie name, leading to XSS.

evidence.note: Query string parameter extracted and decoded
TestCaseNumber derived from class name including parameter
Cookie name printed unescaped to HTML response
